l-001.evidence: The single query (elastic.sshd-auth-history, 10-minute window 09:35–09:45Z on 2026-07-25) returned row_count 0 with an empty values list, so no source.ip/user.name group was surfaced at all. Of the three controls, C-7d (2026-07-18) has window_live false and payload null, so it carries no information; the two live controls disagree — C-21d (2026-07-04, one hour) also returned row_count 0, while C-14d (2026-07-11, one hour) returned exactly one row (accepted 6, failed 0, user.name svc.config-mgmt, source.ip 172.18.0.14) whose first_seen and last_seen are the same instant 09:47:08.297Z, i.e. a single scheduled burst. Since a live one-hour control already returns zero rows, an empty ten-minute observed window is within routine behaviour rather than a stream going dark, so this is not `suppressed`; and with zero observed rows there is nothing that could be distinguishable in accepted, failed, source.ip or user.name.

l-002.evidence: The single query (elastic.syslog-ip-search) over the operation window 2026-07-25T09:35–09:45Z returns row_count 0 with no values, despite the columns (events, data_stream.dataset) being present. Two live controls return a populated baseline for the same host.name == "dev-ws-1": C-14d (window_live: true) has 5 rows — system.auth 444, elastic_agent.metricbeat 360, elastic_agent 12, elastic_agent.filebeat 6, system.syslog 6 — and C-21d (window_live: true) has 5 rows — system.auth 528, metricbeat 360, elastic_agent 14, system.syslog 6, filebeat 4. Even prorating the 60-minute controls to the 10-minute observed window (~74 auth and ~60 metricbeat events expected), the observed count of zero across every dataset means the host stopped emitting entirely; the distinction is carried by the events count per data_stream.dataset. The empty C-7d control is disregarded because window_live is false, but the two live controls are sufficient to establish a non-empty baseline.

l-003.evidence:
The single query (elastic.sshd-auth-history, web-1, 09:35–09:45Z) returned row_count: 0 with the
aggregation columns accepted/failed/source.ip/user.name and an empty values list. Its three controls
do not agree: C-7d (2026-07-18) has window_live: false and a null payload, so it measures nothing;
C-14d (2026-07-11, live) returns 2 rows (svc.config-mgmt 6 accepted/0 failed; svc.reports 0
accepted/72 failed); C-21d (2026-07-04, live) returns row_count: 0 with empty values. With one live
control non-empty and the other live control empty — and both controls widened to 60 minutes against
a 10-minute observation window — the payloads do not establish whether zero sshd auth rows on web-1
is routine (absent) or a dark stream (suppressed). A live, duration-comparable control on web-1 that
consistently returned non-zero accepted/failed rows would have settled it.

l-004.evidence: The lead has a single query, `cmdb.host-trust-edges` with params `{host: dev-ws-1}`, and its observed payload carries only `_note: "state lookup; not an event stream"` plus the echoed params — no event rows, no timestamped columns. The baseline is an empty list because a CMDB lookup carries no `@timestamp` bounds to shift, so no control window exists by construction. Per `state_and_lookup_systems`, cmdb queries return an entity record rather than an event stream and have no baseline-diff semantics. This is `state-only`, not a missing or dead-window measurement, and with only one decidable query there is no cross-query disagreement to record.
